// fold: constant expressions fold at parse time through go/parser,
// go/types and go/constant, with the Go compiler's own arithmetic.
secs := 3*60 + 15;
assert.Equal(tb, "195", fmt.Sprintf("%d", secs));

// The intermediate exceeds int64; go/constant keeps it exact.
big := 1<<70 / (1 << 65);
assert.Equal(tb, "32", fmt.Sprintf("%d", big));

// Constant float arithmetic is exact rationals rounded once, so the
// fold equals float64(0.3), as it does in compiled Go.
tenth := 0.1 + 0.2;
hit := tenth == 0.3;
assert.True(tb, hit);

msg := "a" + "-" + "b";
assert.Equal(tb, "a-b", msg);

neg := -(3 - 5);
assert.Equal(tb, "2", fmt.Sprintf("%d", neg));

mask := (1<<8 - 1) ^ 240;
assert.Equal(tb, "15", fmt.Sprintf("%d", mask));

in := 10%3 == 1 && 7 > 2;
assert.True(tb, in);

// A folded subtree feeds the one runtime operator like any literal.
n := 40;
m := n + 2*1;
assert.Equal(tb, "42", fmt.Sprintf("%d", m));
